| \(\cos \theta\) | \(\frac{35}{37}\) | \(\frac{60}{61}\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) | \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(\frac{20}{29}\) | \(\frac{15}{17}\) | \(\frac{4}{5}\) | \(\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\) |
| \(\tan \theta\) | \(\frac{12}{35}\) | \(\frac{11}{60}\) | \(1\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(\sqrt{2}\) | \(\frac{21}{20}\) | \(\frac{8}{15}\) | \(\frac{3}{4}\) | \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\) |

Method. Where a sine or a cosine is given (columns 1, 2, 4, 5, 8), the partner ratio comes from \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) and then \(\tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\); e.g. in column 1, \(\sin \theta = \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{35}{37}\right)^{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{144}{1369}} = \frac{12}{37}\), so \(\tan \theta = \frac{12}{37} \div \frac{35}{37} = \frac{12}{35}\).

Where a tangent \(\frac{p}{q}\) is given (columns 3, 6, 7, 9), take the opposite side \(= p\) and the adjacent side \(= q\); then the hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{p^{2}+q^{2}}\) and both remaining ratios read straight off the triangle; e.g. in column 9, \(\tan \theta = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\) gives hypotenuse \(\sqrt{1 + 8} = 3\), so \(\sin \theta = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(\cos \theta = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\).

The triples that appear are \((12, 35, 37)\), \((11, 60, 61)\), \((1, 1, \sqrt{2})\), \((1, \sqrt{3}, 2)\), \((\sqrt{2}, 1, \sqrt{3})\), \((21, 20, 29)\), \((8, 15, 17)\), \((3, 4, 5)\) and \((1, 2\sqrt{2}, 3)\).

Equivalent forms of the surd entries: column 3's \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), column 4's \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\), and column 5's \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\) and \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

Substitute \(\tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}\), \(\sin 60^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) and \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\).

\(\frac{\tan 60^{\circ}}{\sin 60^{\circ} + \cos 60^{\circ}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+1}\)

Rationalising by multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}-1\):

\(\frac{2\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}-1)}{(\sqrt{3}+1)(\sqrt{3}-1)} = \frac{2(3-\sqrt{3})}{3-1} = 3 - \sqrt{3}\)

Value \(= 3 - \sqrt{3}\), equivalently \(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+1}\) before rationalising.

Use the identity \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) with \(\sin \theta = \frac{4}{5}\).

\(\cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{2} = 1 - \frac{16}{25} = \frac{9}{25}\)

Since \(\theta\) is an acute angle of a right angled triangle, \(\cos \theta\) is positive, so \(\cos \theta = \sqrt{\frac{9}{25}} = \frac{3}{5}\). (This is the \((3, 4, 5)\) triple.)

\(\cos \theta = \frac{3}{5}\).

Use the identity \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) with \(\cos \theta = \frac{15}{17}\).

\(\sin^{2}\theta = 1 - \left(\frac{15}{17}\right)^{2} = 1 - \frac{225}{289} = \frac{64}{289}\)

Since \(\theta\) is an acute angle of a right angled triangle, \(\sin \theta\) is positive, so \(\sin \theta = \sqrt{\frac{64}{289}} = \frac{8}{17}\). (This is the \((8, 15, 17)\) triple.)

\(\sin \theta = \frac{8}{17}\).
